title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Palpitations and shortness of breath.

HPI
Pt is a 56-year-old female presenting for follow-up of paroxysmal AFib. Pt reports intermittent episodes of rapid heartbeat over the last month. Symptoms typically occur during periods of stress or physical exertion. Pt denies syncope, chest pain, or lightheadedness. Currently managed with rate control medication. Pt reports good adherence to meds.

Medication List
Metoprolol 50mg BID
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Exam
Pt in no acute distress. Alert and oriented x3. BP 122/78, HR 72 (regular), RR 16, Temp 98.6F. Heart: RRR, no murmurs, no rubs. Lungs: CTAB. Extremities: WNL, no edema.

Assessment
1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Currently stable on rate control. Pt has low risk for thromboembolic events; therefore, no anticoagulant is indicated at this time.

Plan
1. Continue Metoprolol 50mg BID for rate control of AFib.
2. Monitor symptoms.
3. F/u in 3 months.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, MD, 05/14/2026

distractors.why: The provider documents paroxysmal, not permanent.
